universities.name: University of Nis Faculty of Medicine
universities.summary: University of Nis Faculty of Medicine has taught medicine since 1960 and runs a direct-entry, six-year English-medium Integrated Academic Studies of Medicine programme, listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools with ECFMG eligibility from 1963 onward. Its accreditor, Serbia's National Accreditation Body, is itself recognized by the World Federation for Medical Education, with accreditation most recently renewed in late 2024.
universities.campusLifestyle: The English-track Medicine programme enrolls up to 120 self-financing international students per year, alongside smaller English-track cohorts in Dental Medicine and Nursing. Teaching combines lectures of up to 80 students with practical groups of 5-10, using a four-level clinical-competence framework that tracks students from theoretical knowledge through to routine performance of clinical skills.
universities.cityProfile: Nis is Serbia's third-largest city and a regional hub in the country's south. The Faculty sits directly adjacent to Clinical Center Nis, the second-largest health institution in Serbia, which reopened in a new facility in December 2017 and serves roughly 3 million people across the wider region.
universities.practicalExposure: The six-year, 360-ECTS curriculum totals 6,030 teaching hours: Years 1-2 cover foundational sciences (anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, immunology, microbiology, medical physics), Year 3 adds pathology, pathophysiology, pharmacology and introductory clinical subjects, and Years 4-6 cover advanced clinical disciplines including internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics/gynecology, psychiatry, neurology, radiology and infectious diseases. Students complete 510 hours of summer clinical practice after Years 3-5, plus a final semester combining 300 hours of clinical internship and a graduation thesis. Clinical training runs at the adjacent Clinical Center Nis and Clinic for Dental Medicine. Graduates receive the Doctor of Medicine (MD) qualification aligned with Serbia's national List of Titles.
universities.hostelOverview: No verified official university accommodation programme for international Medicine-in-English students was found. Applicants should plan to arrange private rental housing independently and confirm current options directly with the Faculty's admissions office (medni.eng@gmail.com) ahead of enrollment.
universities.dietarySupport: No specific on-campus meal plan or dining-cost figure is published for international students. Food costs should be planned as part of an independent living-cost budget alongside private accommodation.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found. International applicants can direct queries to the Faculty's dedicated English-programme admissions contact for day-to-day support.
universities.studentSupport: International admissions run through a dedicated English-programme contact (medni.eng@gmail.com) rather than a general international office. Academic support during the programme includes small practical-group teaching (5-10 students) and a structured, competence-tiered approach to clinical-skills training.

faq.question: Is the Medicine programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. It is an Integrated Academic Studies programme -- admission follows directly from gymnasium, or a 4-year secondary medical or veterinary school, with no separate bachelor's stage required first.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the academic title Doctor of Medicine (MD), aligned with Serbia's national List of Titles under the National Council for Higher Education.

faq.question: How long is the programme and how is it structured?
faq.answer: Six years (360 ECTS credits, 6,030 teaching hours): two years of foundational sciences, a third year adding introductory clinical subjects, and three years of advanced clinical disciplines, plus 510 hours of summer clinical practice and a final-semester 300-hour clinical internship.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: EUR 6,000 per year (EUR 3,000 per semester) for the 2026/27 cohort, confirmed on the Faculty's official Fees and Admissions pages; a EUR 50 application fee also applies (the Admissions page separately lists a EUR 100 fee at registration that has not been reconciled with the EUR 50 figure).

faq.question: What entrance exam does the university require?
faq.answer: A 3-hour written exam in Biology and Chemistry, in English, with a minimum passing score of 21 out of 60 points. There is no standardized-test-based alternative admission route.

faq.question: Is this degree automatically recognized across the EU?
faq.answer: No. Serbia is not an EU member state, so this degree does not carry the automatic EU-wide recognition that an EU-member country's medical degree carries. It is, however, WHO/FAIMER-listed and ECFMG-eligible for US pathways, and noted as acceptable to Canadian medical regulators.

faq.question: When does the academic year start?
faq.answer: The academic year begins 1 October. Applications for the English-medium Medicine track have typically opened in June, with the entrance exam in early July and enrollment by mid-July; confirm exact upcoming-cycle dates directly with the Faculty (medni.eng@gmail.com) closer to the application period.

faq.question: Is university accommodation available for international students?
faq.answer: No verified official university accommodation programme for international Medicine-in-English students was found. Applicants should plan to arrange private rental housing and confirm current options directly with the Faculty.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to join this programme?
faq.answer: The university's own admissions criteria do not reference NEET. Separately, India's National Medical Commission requires Indian citizens and OCI holders who obtain a primary medical qualification abroad to have qualified NEET-UG, whose result serves as the mandatory Eligibility Certificate.

programmes.officialTitle: Integrated Academic Studies of Medicine in English

fee.notes: Officially published 2026/27 tuition: EUR 6,000/year (EUR 3,000/semester) per the Faculty's Fees page, confirmed identically in the 2026/27 enrollment table (120 self-financing English-track seats, no state-funded seats). Total is calculated as the annual figure times 6 years -- not published as a lump sum. A EUR 50 application fee applies; the Admissions page separately lists a EUR 100 fee at the registration stage, unreconciled with the EUR 50 figure. No refund policy was published.

eligibleAudiences: International applicants who have completed gymnasium, a 4-year secondary school of medical orientation, or a 4-year secondary veterinary school
restrictions: Admission is ranked solely on the Faculty's own 3-hour Biology and Chemistry entrance exam (minimum 21/60 to pass) -- no standardized-test-based alternative route is offered
Indian applicants must separately hold a current NEET-UG qualification under India's National Medical Commission rules; this is not administered by the university itself
audienceEligibility.notes: English-language competence certification is required unless the applicant is from a native-English-speaking country.

admissionsContent.overview: Applicants submit documents by email to the Faculty's dedicated English-programme contact, pay the application fee, sit a 3-hour Biology and Chemistry entrance exam, and are ranked on their exam score; accepted candidates then complete registration with further documents and first-semester tuition payment.

eligibility.intro: Admission requires completed secondary education (gymnasium, or a 4-year medical/veterinary secondary school), English-language competence, and a passing score on the Faculty's own entrance exam.
items: High-school completion certificate/diploma with full transcripts, nostrified through Serbia's Ministry of Education process
English-language competence certificate (waived for applicants from native-English-speaking countries)
3-hour written entrance exam in Biology and Chemistry, minimum 21/60 points to pass
Indian applicants: current NEET-UG qualification per India's National Medical Commission rules, separate from the university's own admission process

applicationSteps: Complete the Application form and gather required documents (birth certificate with certified Serbian translation, secondary-school transcripts and diploma with notarized copies, passport copy, English-competence certificate)
Submit documents by email to the Faculty's English-programme admissions contact and pay the EUR 50 application fee
Sit the 3-hour Biology and Chemistry entrance exam on the scheduled date
Check the preliminary and final ranking lists; use the appeals window if needed
If accepted, complete registration (registration form, photographs, Index and ŠV Obrazac forms, first-semester tuition payment, health insurance, student visa)

academic: Original secondary-school transcripts (all years) and High School Diploma, each with notarized copies for the Ministry of Education nostrification process and the Faculty
Ministry of Education certificate confirming nostrification is underway
application: Birth certificate with notarized Serbian translation
